content_of_post_to_comment:
I’ve been constantly trying to sort and fix things with this person and he’s not ready to talk. I had literally put all my blood, swear and tears to solve the fights but nothing is going right.
Whenever I call him to talk and to sort whatever the misunderstandings are… we end up arguing. He just says utmost hurtful things to me, blames me for everything and then cut the call on my face mid conversation without even listening to me and my side and eventually block me. I literally feel soo much desperate to talk to him at that moment but he blocks me from everywhere.
But this doesn’t stop here. Next day he unblocks me but doesn’t wanna talk. What should I understand from this behaviour ??
I have started developing anxiety issues and the fear of losing him haunts me like anything. So I ending end up going to him again, literally beg him to talk and all this make him behave even more brutal with me.
This has been happening from almost a year now and somewhere I know that it’s better set boundaries and maintain distance from him but it’s just I can’t implement it. I feel scared because I feel very lonely and I genuinely don’t have anyone without him.
All this has gone to this extent that it’s affecting my academics and I can’t afford that to happen because I’m in my final year of graduation.
But I can’t bear the pain of losing him either. I feel scared that what if I keep no contacts with him for a few months to let things settle on their own and in that period he finds a replacement or someone better than me that he doesn’t feel the need to have me again in his life ? What if he doesn’t want me anymore after that ? This feeling eats me up every day and is affecting me badly ?
What should I do ? 🙂
comment: The part about him blocking you after saying hurtful things, then unblocking you but refusing to talk, sounds like it has kept you stuck in a cycle of panic and chasing closure. Sometimes the hardest thing to accept is that you can't force a healthy conversation with someone who isn't willing to meet you halfway. Giving space isn't about making him miss you or preventing him from finding someone else; it's about seeing what remains when you're no longer fighting alone for the relationship.
